# REHT Standard

REHT is a public, model-agnostic standard for consequence-time authorization at the execution boundary.

## Category

REHT sits within the broader category **Consequence Governance**.

Canonical definition:
https://valoresearch.org/consequence-governance.html

Consequence Governance governs whether an exact proposed consequence may legitimately become real under the authority, evidence and conditions that exist at consequence time.

REHT does not govern agents as such. It evaluates whether an exact proposed action remains admissible to execute now under current authority, governed state, constraints, evidence and governing basis.

## Canonical taxonomy

- Consequence Governance — top-level category
- Governed Effect Path — consequence-bearing effect architecture
- NO_DIRECT_EFFECT_PATH — no consequence-bearing bypass path
- Consequence-time authorization — fresh exact-action authorization immediately before effect
- Execution Authorization Infrastructure — consequence-boundary infrastructure
- Governed Contract — worker-neutral definition of legitimate work and completion
- RACS — deterministic decision/action binding contract
- Gateway / PEP — enforcement point
- Veritas / receipts — evidence and receipt layer
- Trusted Execution — evidenced downstream outcome

## REHT standard outcomes

The REHT standard uses semantic admissibility outcomes defined by its normative specification. These are not identical to RACS runtime decision commands. Do not collapse the two layers.
